text:
[LLOG.15.1] **Justification linkage is established where the fact is asserted,
not inherited from where the fact came from.** A fact asserted against a
`scope logical` schema (`emit X logical`) is TMS-linked,
**at the asserting tier**, to its justifier activation(s) ([LLOG.1] /
[LLOG.2]); the engine must retract it when the last justifier's LHS no longer
matches. "No longer matches" includes a positive pattern's `within`-recency
window lapsing and a `no`-negation being broken (the cascade case) — the same
justification withdrawal, whatever ends the match. The cross-tier *receiving*
side takes its lifecycle from the receiving schema ([LTIE.9.4], [LLOG.11.7]);
this clause governs only the local assertion.

**A match that ends inside its own firing ends its justification there.**
An action of the firing can end the activation's
own match: a `withdraw` of one of its bindings, an emit that replaces a fact it
matched ([LFAC.2.5.3]), or an emit that breaks one of its `no` patterns. From
that action on the activation justifies nothing. A `logical` fact the firing
emitted before that action loses this justification there, and the engine must
retract it if no other holds it ([LLOG.2.5]). A `logical` fact the firing emits
after that action gains no justification from it, and the engine must retract
it as it is made unless another justification already holds it. [LLOG.11.9]
refuses the shapes a compiler can see. This binds every other, such as an emit
that replaces the matched fact only because two values are equal at run time.

**The `logical` flag restates the schema's lifecycle; it does not select it.**
The author must write the flag on an assertion against a `scope logical` schema
and must not write it on any other ([LLOG.11.1]), so the assertion site carries
no per-fact choice. What makes the linkage local is the tier the assertion
happens in, not anything the emit site decides.

idris.name: ltim_2_7_2__lapsed_fact_retracted
idris.note: 'No longer matches' includes a positive pattern's `within`-recency window lapsing: the justification is withdrawn and the fact retracted at the pump whose sample closes the window. Executed.

idris.name: iret_12_2__queued_successor_removed_timed
idris.note: The justification ends with its match, which a withdraw of the matched fact ends: 'no longer matches'. Executed.

idris.name: llog_3_11_1__clock_where_retracts_timed
idris.note: The justification ends with the match it was made for, and the fact goes with it, at that pump. Executed on the whole engine.

idris.name: ltim_2_7_2__cascade_drops
idris.note: The justification-linkage principle on the cascade: a logical fact whose every justification has ended is retracted, by the engine's cascade, under unique ids.

idris.name: ltim_2_7_2__lapsed_justification_retracted
idris.note: The principle at a tick: a logical fact whose every justifying activation the re-time ended is retracted at that tick, for every program. [LTIM.2.7.2] cites this clause for the retraction; this is the retraction.

idris.name: ltim_2_7_2__retracted_at_the_fixture
idris.note: The principle executed through the theorem: the kind-2 fact, justified by B's ended activation alone, is gone.

idris.name: llog_2_5__strata_composed
idris.note: Executed: composed equals global on the two-strata instance.

idris.name: llog_2_5__strata_upper
idris.note: Executed: an upper stratum retracts what it derived from a lower stratum's retracted fact.

idris.name: llog_2_5__stratified_compose
idris.note: Justification linkage established stratum by stratum composes to the global linkage: the grounded reading of this clause survives recomputation in the SCC-DAG's order.

idris.name: llog_2_5__well_founded
idris.note: The clause's "retract it when the last justifier's LHS no longer matches", read well-foundedly: the least fixpoint of support from the base facts, which is what should be live. Tiers, `within` windows and the `logical` flag are not modelled.
